methods.label: Eliminate the shared expression
methods.explanation:
The first equation gives \(gt=V-V_0\), which lets us remove \(g\) from the second equation without dividing by \(g\) or \(t\). Multiplying the second equation by \(2\), we obtain
\[
2S=gt^2+2V_0t
=t(V-V_0)+2V_0t
=t(V+V_0).
\]
If \(V+V_0\ne0\), we may divide to get
\[
\boxed{t=\frac{2S}{V+V_0}},
\]
which is choice A under this condition.

The zero-denominator case must be considered separately. If \(V+V_0=0\), the equations require \(S=0\) and \(gt=-2V_0\). When \(g\ne0\), this gives \(t=-2V_0/g\). When \(g=0\), consistency requires \(V=V_0=S=0\), and then every \(t\) satisfies both equations.

For example, \(g=2\), \(V_0=-1\), and \(t=1\) give \(V=1\) and \(S=0\). Both original equations hold, but choice A becomes \(0/0\), which is undefined. Thus \(\boxed{\text{A}}\) is the conditional answer; the displayed statement needs the condition \(V+V_0\ne0\).
